The condition is usually caused by mutations in the COL2A1 gene, which provides instructions for making a protein called type II collagen. This protein is essential for the development and maintenance of cartilage and other connective tissue in the body.

In most cases, SED is inherited from a parent who has the condition. If one parent has SED, each child has a 50% chance of inheriting the mutated gene and developing the condition. However, some cases of SED may occur spontaneously, without a family history of the condition.

There are several types of SED, and the inheritance pattern may vary depending on the specific type. Some types of SED may be inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, which means that a person needs to inherit two copies of the mutated gene (one from each parent) to develop the condition.
